method: OPEN AND QUOTED from European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline' (2022). Source text: NCBI efetch JATS XML (Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 503 on 2026-09-23). Tables 3–5 (oestrogen, testosterone and gonadotropin regimens) were stripped.

claims.claim: **Boys:** refer for expert assessment if puberty is delayed (puberty SD score below −2), there are no signs of puberty by age 14, or puberty is not progressing.
claims.source_text: R. 3.1We recommend expert evaluation of puberty in any boy who has delayed puberty as defined by a puberty s.d. score <-2 or no signs of puberty at the age of 14 years or fails to show adequate progression in puberty.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Girls:** refer if there are no signs of puberty by age 13 or the puberty SD score is below −2. Girls with a condition that puts them at risk of hypogonadism should be assessed from age 8; at-risk boys from age 9.
claims.source_text: R. 2.1We recommend that an expert evaluation should be performed on any girl who does not show any sign of puberty by the age of 13 years, any girl who, by some definition, has delayed puberty (puberty s.d. score <-2) and all girls with a known condition/diagnosis that poses a risk of hypogonadism from the age of 8 years. … R 3.2All boys with a history of a condition that places them at risk of hypogonadism should undergo pubertal assessment from the age of 9 years.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment belongs with a multidisciplinary team** (paediatric and adult endocrinology, psychology, urology, gynaecology, genetics, nursing, as needed).
claims.source_text: R 1.1We recommend that children and adolescents who need pubertal induction or sex hormone replacement to sustain puberty should be treated by a multidisciplinary team including a paediatric endocrinologist, adult endocrinologist, psychologist, urologist, gynaecologist, geneticist, surgeon and nurse specialist depending on the situation and specific requirements.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CDGP is the commonest cause of delayed puberty in boys (about 63%)**, and in most cases (50–75%) a parent also had late puberty. In girls it accounts for about a third of cases.
claims.source_text: CDGP is the most common cause of delayed puberty in teenage boys (~63%), with a majority (50-75%) of them having at least one parent with a history of delayed puberty … CDGP is responsible for a third of all cases of pubertal delay in teenage girls () and is mainly considered as part of the spectrum of normal puberty.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CDGP is a diagnosis of exclusion:** rule out congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH), primary gonadal failure, chronic illness and tumours. It is confirmed only when puberty then progresses on its own.
claims.source_text: The diagnosis of CDGP can only be made after exclusion of conditions such as CHH or primary gonadal failure that leads to permanent hypogonadism, as well as chronic illnesses, or a tumour that may lead to a variable extent of delayed growth and puberty … Clinically, CDGP is transient and confirmed by a spontaneous progression of puberty.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Clues to CHH rather than CDGP:** cryptorchidism (especially bilateral), micropenis, midline defects, reduced or absent smell, deafness, or kidney anomalies.
claims.source_text: A history of cryptorchidism (especially bilateral), micro-penis, midline defects, hypo or anosmia, deafness or renal anomalies increases the likelihood of CHH.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assessment includes** history (including family timing of puberty), Tanner stage and testicular volume by orchidometer, growth velocity, gonadotropins and sex steroids, and bone age. Consider a karyotype or microarray in boys with high gonadotropins, atypical genitalia, malformations or features of a sex-chromosome disorder.
claims.source_text: Clinically, the pubertal stage is measured by scoring Tanner stages and testis volume using a Prader orchidometer. Growth velocity, biochemical testing of gonadotropins and sex steroids and radiological evaluation of bone age by X-ray of the left hand give additional information. The family history on the timing of pubertal development is essential in the evaluation process. … Thus, boys with delayed puberty and a past history of atypical genitalia, congenital malformations, hypergonadotropic hypogonadism or clinical features of sex chromosome disorders should also have a karyotype or a chromosomal microarray.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When CHH and CDGP cannot be told apart,** it may be necessary to wait beyond age 14 before starting induction. In girls, rule out spontaneous puberty and treatable causes first.
claims.source_text: For this reason, in patients with pubertal delay and uncertainty regarding the diagnosis of CHH or CDGP, it may sometime be necessary to delay the initiation of induction even beyond 14 years. … R 2.3We recommend that spontaneous puberty and treatable causes of hypogonadism should be ruled out before starting puberty induction in girls.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **All boys with permanent hypogonadism should have pubertal induction,** started by age 12 if there is no pubertal development and the diagnosis carries a high risk of hypogonadism.
claims.source_text: R. 3.3We recommend that all boys with permanent hypogonadism should undergo pubertal induction. … R. 3.4In boys who are known to have a diagnosis with a high risk of hypogonadism, we recommend that pubertal induction can be started by the age of 12 years if there are no signs of pubertal development. (+OOO)
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Induce with testosterone, starting low and increasing gradually to the adult dose,** for example testosterone enanthate 50 mg monthly, transdermal testosterone 10 mg every other day, or oral testosterone undecanoate 40 mg daily.
claims.source_text: R. 3.5We recommend that pubertal induction in boys with hypogonadism should be performed with testosterone (++OO) … It is common to begin treatment with low-dose testosterone (i.e. 50 mg testosterone enanthate every month, 10 mg transdermal testosterone every other day or 40 mg oral testosterone undecanoate daily) and then gradually increase to the adult dose.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use long-acting testosterone undecanoate injection to start puberty:** it can advance bone age too fast and cut final height.
claims.source_text: Testosterone undecanoate, the long-acting preparation, should not be used for induction of puberty or progression through the early stages of puberty, as it is likely to advance bone age too rapidly with a potential for truncating final height.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Late-diagnosed young men with CHH** are often started on higher doses (testosterone enanthate 200–250 mg monthly, then every 2–3 weeks) for faster virilisation.
claims.source_text: Adult endocrinologists often see patients with CHH in late adolescence or early adulthood with the main complaint of lack of pubertal development (). In such cases, the therapeutic approach is often more incisive than for younger patients, involving higher initial testosterone doses than those used by paediatric endocrinologists (200-250mg testosterone enanthate monthly, then every 2-3 weeks) to induce more rapid virilisation
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor every 3–6 months:** pubertal and skeletal maturation and height velocity, plus local reactions, gynaecomastia, priapism, haematocrit, liver function and behaviour.
claims.source_text: Regular clinical follow-up is generally performed every 3-6 months to assess the effectiveness of testosterone therapy by assessing pubertal and skeletal maturation and height velocity. … It should include the assessment of adverse signs such as local reactions, gynaecomastia, priapism, increased haematocrit, deranged liver function and inappropriate behavioural changes.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Watch for gynaecomastia:** it occurs in up to a third of boys on gonadotropins or testosterone, usually at too-high doses, and often reverses when the dose is adjusted.
claims.source_text: Gynaecomastia occurs in up to a third of patients on gonadotropins () or testosterone () and usually (although not invariably) occurs during supraphysiological replacement doses. The risk and severity of gynaecomastia can be reversed by adjusting the dosage.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In boys with HH, discuss both options:** testosterone or gonadotropins. Neither is proven better for virilisation; the choice depends on preference, ease of use, availability and fertility plans.
claims.source_text: R 4.1We suggest discussing two treatment options for pubertal induction in boys with secondary hypogonadism: testosterone or gonadotropins. … There is no clear evidence that one regimen is superior to another and there is no clear evidence that supports the preferential use of any of these regimens instead of testosterone replacement for the purpose of achieving virilisation in boys with HH. The preparations used will depend on the preferences of the patient, ease of use as well as local availability and if fertility is considered.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Testosterone virilises but does not grow the testes or start sperm production;** gonadotropins can.
claims.source_text: Although effective in inducing pubertal signs and symptoms, testosterone formulations neither stimulate testicular growth nor will they induce spermatogenesis. … Alternatively, a potential testicular development and fertility in males with HH can be achieved with puberty induction through the use of gonadotropins
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **hCG can be used alone or with recombinant FSH,** but the combination works much better for testicular growth and sperm production. FSH pre-treatment before hCG may be better still. Gonadotropins need several injections a week.
claims.source_text: exogenous hCG alone or in combination with recombinant FSH (, ). However, consistent evidence suggests that the combination therapy with recombinant FSH (rFSH)/hCG is significantly more effective than hCG alone both for inducing spermatogenesis and increasing testicular volume. … some evidence suggests that a pre-treatment with rFSH followed by the combination with hCG or GnRH is even more effective in optimising the Sertoli cell maturation … Treatment with gonadotropins, whatever the protocol used, requires multiple weekly injections
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Combined FSH/hCG for 6–24 months** grows the testes in almost all boys and produces sperm in 80–95% of those without undescended testes. Before switching to testosterone, do a semen analysis and consider sperm banking.
claims.source_text: The combination of rFSH and hCG therapy for 6-24 months results in testicular growth in almost all and spermatogenesis in 80-95% of patients without undescended testes … The shift from FSH/hCG therapy to testosterone should occur after sperm analysis, and in the case of sufficient sperm in the ejaculate, sperm cryopreservation (banking) should be considered, particularly in severe oligospermia.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CHH can reverse in 5–20%,** so a short break (about 4 months) after gonadotropin induction and before testosterone may be considered to check for recovery.
claims.source_text: since 'reversal' of CHH has been described () in 5-20% of patients with CHH, a brief therapy withdrawal (i.e. 4 months) after the conclusion of pubertal induction with gonadotropins and before the start of TRT might be considered in order to verify a spontaneous recovery of the HPG axis.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start induction at about 11 when hypogonadism is confirmed and there are no signs of puberty, or at 13 if constitutional delay is suspected.** For CDGP, a short 3–6 month course of low-dose oestradiol may be used, with monitoring for spontaneous progress.
claims.source_text: R. 2.4We recommend to start individualised puberty induction in girls at the age of 11 years in cases where there are no signs of pubertal development and a diagnosis of hypogonadism is confirmed, or at the age of 13 years if the constitutional delay is suspected. … In case of CDGP, treatment may be initiated as a short course of 3-6 months using low doses of oestradiol. Doses can be increased in order to mimic the normal course of puberty, but continuous monitoring for spontaneous resumption of progress and gonadotropin secretion is required.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use 17β-oestradiol** (oral or transdermal) rather than ethinyl oestradiol or conjugated oestrogens, and titrate the dose to pubertal progress.
claims.source_text: R 2.6We recommend to use 17β-oestradiol for puberty induction or to sustain puberty in girls (++OO). … Oestrogens can be used orally or transdermally for puberty induction. … R 2.8We suggest titrating/adjusting the oestrogen therapy dose based on the appropriate progression of puberty during puberty induction or sex hormone replacement in girls. (+OOO)
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review at least every 3–6 months** (weight, height, blood pressure, Tanner stage). Add progesterone after breakthrough bleeding or after at least 2 years, then move to adult hormone replacement.
claims.source_text: R 2.7We recommend a follow-up frequency with a minimum of once every 3-6 months during pubertal induction or sex hormone replacement to sustain puberty in girls. … R 2.9We recommend that progesterone is added after puberty induction or during sex hormone replacement to sustain puberty in girls after breakthrough bleeding, after at least 2 years of treatment. (+OOO) … R 2.10We recommend to change pubertal induction treatment of oestrogen and progesterone to permanent adult sex hormone replacement therapy at the end of pubertal induction.
claims.locator: European Reference Network on Rare Endocrine Conditions (Endo-ERN) (Nordenström A et al.), European Journal of Endocrinology, 'Pubertal induction and transition to adult sex hormone replacement in patients with congenital pituitary or gonadal reproductive hormone deficiency: an Endo-ERN clinical practice guideline', 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9066594/, retrieved 2026-09-23
